title: compass_app: layers, wiring and how the Home screen gets its data
intro: You will be able to place any file of compass_app in its layer (ui, domain, data), explain how the development and staging entry points swap Local and Remote repositories, and trace the Home screen from the go_router route to ApiClient and back into a ListenableBuilder. You will also know how the tests substitute fakes at the same seams.
subject: The big picture: how the app is layered and how a screen gets its data
docsNote: The README only mentions architecture in passing and never describes the ui/domain/data folders. A short architecture page mapping each folder to its role would help newcomers.

chapters.title: The layer map: ui, domain, data
chapters.goal: Place files of app/lib in the ui, domain or data layer, and say what each layer owns: screens and view models, models and use cases, repositories and services (ApiClient, LocalDataService).
chapters.hootIntro: Under app/lib, Compass splits into ui, domain and data folders, and each file's imports tell you which layer it belongs to.

steps.title: Three folders, three jobs
steps.body: The README says this app exists to explain Flutter architecture. `app/lib` reflects that with `ui/`, `domain/` and `data/` folders, plus `config/` (dependencies.dart, assets.dart), `routing/` (router.dart, routes.dart), `utils/` (Result, Command) and the entry points `main*.dart`. The ui layer holds screens (`widgets/`) and view models (`view_models/`) per feature. The domain layer holds models and use cases. The data layer holds repositories and services.

sources.why: States the app is used to explain architecture
Imports show ui depending on data repositories and domain models

steps.title: Place the files
steps.prompt: Match each file to the layer folder it lives in.

pairs.right: data layer: a service talking HTTP

steps.explanation: The folder tells the layer, and the sub-folder tells the role: widgets and view_models in ui, models and use_cases in domain, repositories and services in data.

stops.annotation: A ui class. HomeViewModel is a `ChangeNotifier` that receives `BookingRepository` and `UserRepository` and exposes `load` and `deleteBooking` commands. It holds screen state, not fetching code.
A domain model: a freezed class with id, name, startDate, endDate. Its doc says it carries just what the home screen needs; the full `Booking` comes from the repository.
A data-layer contract. The abstract `BookingRepository` returns domain types wrapped in `Result`, never API or JSON types.
A service: LocalDataService loads JSON assets via `rootBundle` and decodes them into domain models like Activity and Destination.

steps.title: What the domain layer owns
steps.body: Domain holds the app's vocabulary: freezed models such as `BookingSummary`, `Booking`, `Destination`, `Activity` and `User`, with generated `.freezed.dart` and `.g.dart` files you never edit. It also holds use cases. `BookingCreateUseCase` takes `DestinationRepository`, `ActivityRepository` and `BookingRepository`, checks the `ItineraryConfig` for destination, activities and dates, then builds and saves a `Booking`. This is logic that spans several repositories, so it fits neither one repository nor a view model.

steps.title: Where the data layer touches the network
steps.prompt: Click the line that makes ApiClient return a failure result instead of throwing when a request errors.
steps.explanation: Each ApiClient method wraps its work in try/catch and returns `Result.error(error)`. Callers in repositories and view models then switch on Ok/Error instead of handling exceptions.

steps.question: BookingRepositoryRemote converts a BookingApiModel into domain types. Which layer does BookingApiModel belong to?
choices: Data, under services/api/model, next to ApiClient
Domain, under models/booking, next to Booking
Ui, under home/view_models, next to HomeViewModel
Config, under config, next to dependencies.dart
steps.hint: Look at the folder path of booking_api_model.freezed.dart.
steps.explanation: BookingApiModel lives in `data/services/api/model/booking`. It is the wire shape; the repository maps it to domain models so the layers above never see it.

sources.why: Repository builds a BookingApiModel from a domain Booking

takeaways: ui owns screens (widgets/) and view models like HomeViewModel; it depends on repository interfaces and domain models.
domain owns models such as BookingSummary and use cases such as BookingCreateUseCase.
data owns repositories (BookingRepository) and services (ApiClient, LocalDataService), including API models such as BookingApiModel.

chapters.title: One interface, two implementations: Local vs Remote
chapters.goal: Explain how BookingRepository is implemented by BookingRepositoryLocal (LocalDataService, JSON assets) and BookingRepositoryRemote (ApiClient plus BookingApiModel mapping to BookingSummary), and why the ui never sees the difference.

chapters.title: Wiring it up: entry points and dependencies.dart
chapters.goal: Show how main_development.dart and main_staging.dart choose providersLocal or providersRemote in config/dependencies.dart, and how context.read() resolves a repository by its abstract type for the router and use cases.

chapters.title: Following the Home screen: route, ViewModel, Command, widget
chapters.goal: Trace /home from the GoRoute in router.dart through HomeScreenContainer and HomeViewModel.load (Command0, Result) to the ListenableBuilder in HomeScreen, and explain how the same screen is tested with FakeBookingRepository in home_screen_test.dart.
